title: Projectile Motion: Which Angle Flies Farthest?
subtitle: 同速、同高、无空气阻力
sourceTitle: An original lesson: three launch angles

scenes.title: Change only the angle
scenes.narration: Same height, same speed, three launch angles. At 30, 45 or 60 degrees, which goes farthest?
scenes.sourceQuote: Same height, same speed, three launch angles. At 30, 45 or 60 degrees, which goes farthest?

props.headline: Only the angle changes
descriptions: The angle changes height and flight time.

scenes.title: Lock the conditions first
scenes.narration: Each ball leaves at 10 meters per second. Gravity is 10 meters per second squared. Air drag is ignored, and the ground is level.
scenes.sourceQuote: Each ball leaves at 10 meters per second. Gravity is 10 meters per second squared. Air drag is ignored, and the ground is level.

props.headline: Same speed · height · no drag
descriptions: The angle changes height and flight time.

scenes.title: Three paths in flight
scenes.narration: At 30 degrees it stays low, at 60 it climbs. Airtimes differ, but both land in one spot.
scenes.sourceQuote: At 30 degrees it stays low, at 60 it climbs. Airtimes differ, but both land in one spot.

props.headline: Low and high, same landing
descriptions: The angle changes height and flight time.

scenes.title: 45 degrees lands farther
scenes.narration: The 45-degree path lands farther. It covers 10 meters horizontally. The other two reach about 8.66 meters.
scenes.sourceQuote: The 45-degree path lands farther. It covers 10 meters horizontally. The other two reach about 8.66 meters.

props.headline: 45° reaches 10 m
descriptions: The angle changes height and flight time.

scenes.title: Why 45 degrees wins
scenes.narration: Range follows the sine of twice the angle. As 30 and 60 sum to 90, their ranges match. In this setup, 45 degrees goes farthest.
scenes.sourceQuote: Range follows the sine of twice the angle. As 30 and 60 sum to 90, their ranges match. In this setup, 45 degrees goes farthest.

props.headline: Double the angle, then take the sine
descriptions: The angle changes height and flight time.
